_help.about: [NOT WIRED YET — design §DK; hidden is wired, §DJ] The hidden places off the road, and the shrine with the sealed scroll (3 Oct, Mike by voice). First guesses by Claude (chat), 3 Oct; the designer owns them. Restart after editing.
_help.hidden: §DJ. Hand-made set pieces that the generator places where they fit (§CJ.8: nothing is hand-placed on a generated planet), never on a road: off_road_m from the nearest one, just far enough that you choose to lose sight of it (§BC). per_km_of_road: about how many to a kilometre of road, on either side. kits: Mike's first three, what each is and what its site needs; more kits later. speakers_share: how many hidden places have one of the few who speak (§DJ): a small figure on the shared rig with a line for the log. A hidden place with a hearth is a hearth like any other for §CU's count and §CV's smoke.
_help.shrine: §DK. A new monument kind. An ominous hallway goes down into the ground (or in under a great tree's roots, kits.oak_door), wall torches burning along it in sconces, and at its end an altar with a sealed scroll. Its delve (§CJ: every ruin has one) is shut behind the altar until the sconces are set to the scroll's pattern. A sconce is a torch in a bracket: put out by hand (sconce_snuff: interact, right click smothers it), lit again with your torch's swing (sconce_relight: swing, §CN), with no kindling (laying is for fires). Sconces never smoke (§CV). sconces: how many (a range). pattern: which are lit and which dark, seeded per shrine; never all lit (how you find it) and never all dark. open: what moves when the hall matches the pattern: the wall behind the altar gives way to steps going down. light: what the sconces burn with, open for Mike (ordinary fire someone tends unseen, or a stranger light that isn't fire); either way they are burning when you first come.
_help.scroll: §DK. The sealed scroll (items.json scroll). Only some can read its marks and break its seal (readers: open for Mike), somewhere else, down the road or elsewhere in the same biome, reader_far_km from the shrine, never at the shrine. Shown to anyone else it comes back (log.shown). The reader asks first (log.asked_where), then reads it: a passage of old wisdom (public domain, as the tomes, §DL) and the pattern, both kept whole in the log (hud.json log_more). The text never names how the shrine's people ended (§BQ). Guessing the pattern at the door is possible but costly: every sconce you put out is dark you made yourself (§BA), and the hall is long enough that walking to a reader is the better way.
_help.lines: hidden.lines: what the few who speak say (§DJ), one line picked per figure per visit, into the log as 'spoken'. First guesses by Claude Code, 4 Oct: short, strange, no names, no instructions, no quest text. Mike replaces them.
_help.hidden_built: Built 4 Oct (§DJ, scripts/landmarks/hidden_places.gd): each road link offers per_km_of_road × its length in places (14 tries each), off_road_m from it, each kit tried in a seeded order where its site fits; a place stands only if no road passes within off_road_m[0]. earth_homes: a bank (slope 0.12-0.7), flat ground 9 m in front for the hearth, water within 500 m, a forest biome here or next door; two to four doors; the camp is Camps' under the camp sim. oak_door: a rise 3 m over the ground 120 m round, an oak where an oak passes the place's gate, else its tallest broadleaf, 1.12 × the top of its band. burning_shrine: a slope of 0.25 within 10 m. A hidden place's hearth is added to §CU's count, not dealt into it.

kits.what: A hidden grove with homes dug into a bank under the turf (Mike's 'hobbit-style homes', built from the real turf-house, earth-lodge and pit-house ways, our own folklore and not Tolkien's, §BO): a small camp under §BL's rules, with its own hearth.
kits.needs: a sheltered hollow or bank, water near, woods in reach

kits.what: A shrine's door under a great gnarled old tree on a rise: its roots grip a stone doorway that goes down.
kits.needs: an old broadleaf of that place past the top of its size band (an oak where oaks grow, §CA, §CS), on a rise

kits.what: An abandoned shrine whose torches still burn, going down into the ground (the shrine, below).
kits.needs: rock or a slope to go into

lines: The roots remember the rain before this one.
You walk loud for someone so far from home.
Every door here opens downward, in the end.
The moon counted you twice last night.
Stones keep what is said near them.
Not everything that burns is fire.
The road forgets its feet. We do not.
Ash is only wood that has finished thinking.
Some lights are lit to be found, and some to be followed.
You came the long way. Good.

log.taken: You took the scroll from the altar. The seal holds, and the marks mean nothing to you.
log.shown: They turn the scroll over and hand it back.
log.opened: The wall behind the altar gives way. Steps go down.
